def _compute_cid(packets: list[DirectivePacket], model: str) -> str:
    """Compute a deterministic composition identity hash."""
    components = [
        f"{p.layer}:{p.name}:{len(p.text)}" for p in packets
    ]
    components.append(f"model:{model}")
    raw = "|".join(components)
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
==== REPLACE
def _compute_cid(packets: list[DirectivePacket], model: str) -> str:
    """Compute a deterministic composition identity hash."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for p in packets:
        h.update(f"{p.layer}:{p.name}:".encode())
        h.update(p.text.encode())
        h.update(b"|")
    h.update(f"model:{model}".encode())
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]

findings.description:
`bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py::_prune_for_coherence()` uses a density formula that pruning cannot improve under its current numerator.

The function computes:
constraint_count = _count_constraints(policy)
density = constraint_count / token_estimate
Then, after pruning text, it recomputes:
remaining_tokens = max(remaining_chars // 4, 1)
density = constraint_count / remaining_tokens
But `constraint_count` is fixed from the TOML policy and is not reduced when SOFT packet text or SOFT directive blocks are removed.

Evidence:

For positive `constraint_count`, if pruning reduces `remaining_tokens`, then:
constraint_count / remaining_tokens
increases.

Concrete arithmetic:
constraint_count = 10
tokens_before = 1000
